claim: The findings are based on the direct crystallographic analysis of seven distinct bHLH family members (ARNT, HIF-1α, HIF-2α, NPAS1, NPAS3, CLOCK and BMAL1).
source: Our findings are based on the direct crystallographic analysis of seven distinct bHLH family members (ARNT, HIF-1α, HIF-2α, NPAS1, NPAS3, CLOCK and BMAL1).
evidence: This summarizes the structural work presented in the manuscript.

claim: In all seven crystallographically examined bHLH-PAS proteins, internal hydrophobic cavities were clearly observed within both their PAS-A and PAS-B domains.
source: In all these proteins, internal hydrophobic cavities were clearly observed within both their PAS-A and PAS-B domains.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the crystal structures.

claim: PAS domains become interweaved in bHLH-PAS heterodimers through at least two highly distinct forms of architecture.
source: These PAS domains become interweaved in bHLH-PAS heterodimers through at least two highly distinct forms of architecture.
evidence: This is based on structural comparisons showing differences between ARNT-based and BMAL1-based heterodimers.

claim: AHR has ligand-binding capabilities.
source: Aside from the seven members we crystallographically examined, three additional members: AHR (Stejskalova et al., 2011)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: HIF-3α has ligand-binding capabilities.
source: HIF-3α (Fala et al., 2015)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: NPAS2 has ligand-binding capabilities.
source: and NPAS2 (Dioum et al., 2002) are known to have ligand-binding capabilities associated with at least one of their PAS domains
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Ten bHLH-PAS family members have experimentally confirmed ligand-binding pockets.
source: bringing the experimentally confirmed number of ligand pocket containing members to ten.
evidence: This is a count based on the seven crystallographically examined proteins plus three with known ligand-binding capabilities.

claim: ARNT2, SIM1 and SIM2 are likely to harbor pockets due to considerable amino-acid conservations with ARNT and NPAS1.
source: Our sequence-structure comparative analyses further implicate three more members: ARNT2, SIM1 and SIM2, as likely to harbor pockets due to considerable amino-acid conservations with ARNT and NPAS1.
evidence: This is an inference based on sequence conservation analysis.

claim: The discovery of ligand-binding cavities in bHLH-PAS proteins should fuel the future search for their physiological and endogenous ligands.
source: Our unmasking of the wider bHLH-PAS protein family as a group of transcription factors with multi-ligand-binding capabilities should fuel the future search for their physiological and endogenous ligands.
evidence: This is a speculation about future research directions based on the findings.

claim: The protein pockets make bHLH-PAS factors ideally suited for applications of high-throughput screening campaigns to find small-molecule therapeutics for a variety of human diseases.
source: The protein pockets, in each case, make these factors ideally suited for applications of high-throughput screening campaigns to find small-molecule therapeutics for a variety of human diseases, including psychiatric illnesses, cancers and metabolic diseases.
evidence: This is a speculation about therapeutic applications based on the structural findings.

claim: The distinctive amino-acid residues inside bHLH-PAS pockets predict successful outcomes for screens seeking highly selective modulators for each protein.
source: The distinctive amino-acid residues inside their pockets predict successful outcomes for screens seeking highly selective modulators for each protein.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural diversity of the pockets.

claim: bHLH-PAS pockets are highly pliable and can accommodate significantly larger ligands than their empty volumes alone suggest.
source: These pockets are also highly pliable and can accommodate significantly larger ligands than their empty volumes alone suggest.
evidence: This is based on the observation that ligand binding can expand pocket size.

claim: The precise mechanism through which endogenous and/or pharmacologic ligands can modulate transcriptional activities of bHLH-PAS proteins has not yet been fully revealed.
source: The precise mechanism through which endogenous and/or pharmacologic ligands can modulate transcriptional activities of bHLH-PAS proteins has not yet been fully revealed
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge.

claim: The mechanism of ligand modulation could differ for each bHLH-PAS family member.
source: and could differ for each family member.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the diversity of the family.

claim: Ligand binding to AHR can displace heat shock protein 90 and initiate the nuclear translocation of AHR.
source: For example, ligand binding to AHR can displace heat shock protein 90 and initiate the nuclear translocation of AHR (Soshilov and Denison, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: Some small-molecule HIF-2α antagonists that bind to the PAS-B domain can disrupt the dimerization between HIF-2α and ARNT.
source: Some small-molecule HIF-2α antagonists that bind to the PAS-B domain can disrupt the dimerization between HIF-2α and ARNT (Scheuermann et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior literature.

claim: The mechanistic links between ligand binding and transcriptional regulation in bHLH-PAS proteins remain to be discovered.
source: Beyond these initial observations to date, and without the availability of small-molecule tools to probe other bHLH-PAS proteins, the mechanistic links between ligand binding and transcriptional regulation remain to be discovered.
evidence: This is a statement about gaps in current knowledge.

claim: Dimeric nuclear receptors harbor two pockets in their functional architectures.
source: It is interesting that while dimeric nuclear receptors harbor two pockets in their functional architectures
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of nuclear receptor structure.

claim: bHLH-PAS proteins present four distinct pockets in their functional architectures.
source: the bHLH-PAS proteins present four distinct pockets.
evidence: This is based on the structural findings presented in the manuscript.

claim: A fifth pocket was observed in HIF-2α-ARNT heterodimers, located between two subunits, allowing proflavine to promote subunit dissociation.
source: Notably a fifth pocket was also observed in HIF-2α-ARNT heterodimers, located between two subunits, allowing proflavine to promote subunit dissociation (Wu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on the authors' prior work.

claim: Crevices formed between the PAS domains within the quaternary architectures of bHLH-PAS family members could form additional ligand binding and modulation sites.
source: The latter finding further suggests that crevices formed between the PAS domains within the quaternary architectures of family members could form additional ligand binding and modulation sites.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of the fifth pocket in HIF-2α-ARNT.

claim: The availability of many distinctive pockets within bHLH-PAS proteins could allow a variety of biosynthetic or metabolic signals derived from cellular pathways to be integrated into a single unified functional response.
source: The availability of so many distinctive pockets within bHLH-PAS proteins could allow a variety of biosynthetic or metabolic signals derived from cellular pathways to be integrated into a single unified functional response.
evidence: This is a speculation about the functional significance of multiple pockets.

claim: Each pocket may allow a bHLH-PAS protein to be the site of unique ligand within each cell-type.
source: Alternatively, each pocket may allow a bHLH-PAS protein to be the site of unique ligand within each cell-type.
evidence: This is a speculation about the functional significance of multiple pockets.

claim: The identification and validation of endogenous ligands for bHLH-PAS proteins will help define the genetic programs controlled by each member.
source: The identification and validation of endogenous ligands for this family will help define the genetic programs controlled by each bHLH-PAS member.
evidence: This is a speculation about future research directions.

claim: Multiple classes of ligands, including halogenated aromatic hydrocarbons, tetrapyrroles and several tryptophan derivatives were previously identified as direct AHR binding ligands.
source: Interestingly, multiple classes of ligands, including halogenated aromatic hydrocarbons, tetrapyrroles and several tryptophan derivatives were previously identified as direct AHR binding ligands (Denison et al., 2011; Stejskalova et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: AHR ligands display significant variations in their chemical structures and sizes, but still bind with high affinities to AHR (Kd values of 0.1–100 nM).
source: These molecules display significant variations in their chemical structures and sizes, but still bind with high affinities to AHR (Kd values of 0.1–100 nM).
evidence: This is based on prior literature about AHR ligands.

claim: High-affinity, multi-ligand binding by AHR can best be accounted for by the use of four discrete pockets within AHR-ARNT.
source: High-affinity, multi-ligand binding can best be accounted for by the use of four discrete pockets within AHR-ARNT, as shown here for other ARNT heterodimers, than just one pocket as suggested previously (Pandini et al., 2007).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural findings and comparison with prior models.

claim: The Kd value of NPAS1-ARNT binding to HRE DNA was 16.3 ± 1.1 nM.
source: The Kd values of NPAS1-ARNT and NPAS3-ARNT binding to the same HRE element were 16.3 ± 1.1 nM and 17.5 ± 1.1 nM, as calculated from three technical replicates respectively.
evidence: This is experimental data from fluorescence anisotropy measurements shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The Kd value of NPAS3-ARNT binding to HRE DNA was 17.5 ± 1.1 nM.
